admin.integrity.intro: v1.9.8 anti-abuse controls. The playback-credit gate (80% real-watch required, position seeks excluded, items under 60s rejected as prerolls) is always on. The two settings below add a daily soft-cap and an audit-log flag for users hitting unusual rates. Test tools at the bottom let you verify both fire without waiting for real users to game the system.
admin.integrity.cap_value: Daily cap (items per user per UTC day):
admin.integrity.cap_hint: Real users never hit this. Default 200.
admin.integrity.rate_threshold: Flag threshold (items credited per rolling hour):
admin.integrity.rate_hint: Doesn't block; just records "suspicious_rate" in the audit log. Throttled to once per user per hour.
admin.integrity.test_intro: Inject N fake credited playbacks into a test user's account. Real path: each event passes the 80% gate, then the cap and rate flag decide what lands. Use this on a throwaway test user to verify caps work before relying on them.
admin.integrity.revoke_intro: Un-award a specific badge from a specific user. Useful when a user was found to have gamed a badge before integrity fixes landed. Audit-logged as "admin_revoke_badge".
admin.integrity.revoke_hint: Badge ids show in the user's profile JSON or the badge catalog.
admin.v2test.intro: Grant score, power-ups, or cosmetics to a user without waiting for real watch progress. Useful for verifying the Loadout UI on a test profile or backfilling milestone titles after the v2.0 release.
admin.v2test.user_id_hint: Find the user GUID via Jellyfin Admin → Users → click a user; their GUID is in the URL.
admin.v2test.backfill_intro: Iterates every known profile and runs the v2.0 shop milestone check against their LifetimeScore. Users already past Cinephile (1000) / Marathoner (2500) / Curator (5000) get those rank titles auto-granted now instead of waiting for their next watch event. Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.
admin.fc.audiobook_note: Controls whether an audiobook play credits your Book badges, Music badges, or both. Pure music tracks always count as music; ebooks always count as books.
